Subject: On-prem deployment kickoff — topology & constraints

Hi Hiro,

Thanks again for taking the time today. As discussed, Anchorage Health is evaluating a multi-tenant on-prem deployment for Redwood Private in our primary datacenter. High-level constraints that matter to us:

- Two physical racks in separate rooms (latency ~800us between racks)
- No internet egress for inference traffic (control plane can reach Redwood over a management VLAN)
- Hardware: 8x A100-style GPUs (4 per rack) initially; room to add 4 GPUs per rack in future
- Dataset retention requirements: 90 days, nightly backup to an internal object-store

Attached is a rough facility diagram and an inventory sheet for the nodes (anchorage-network-diagram.pdf, node-profiles-anchorage.xlsx).

Primary asks for the next week:
1) Proposed cluster node-pool layout and failure domains
2) Storage architecture for KV cache + model artifacts (fast local NVMe vs shared blockstore)
3) Any gating items for air-gapped operations (we currently have a management VLAN with limited egress)

Can we get a short plan/notes from your infra team by end of week? I can make time for a technical review on Thursday afternoon.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Platform Engineering
Anchorage Health

Tom — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We're happy to own the design proposal. Quick high-level response:

- Node-pools: plan to split into inference (GPU) pools and control/infra pools. For inference, recommend 2 node pools (rack-aware): 
  * gp-infer-rack-a (4 GPUs)
  * gp-infer-rack-b (4 GPUs)
  This gives us a simple failure-domain boundary and keeps KV cache local to the rack where possible.

- Storage: prefer local NVMe for model shards and KV cache to keep token-latency tight, with periodic sync to your internal object-store for durability. We'll propose a fallback to shared iSCSI blockstore for model uploads if NVMe capacity is insufficient.

- Airgap: we have a private-control-plane mode that works over an HTTPS management channel on your management VLAN. For fully air-gapped operations (no egress), we will need an offline package and a short soft-lease period for telemetry. We'll list the specific gating items in the technical note.

I'll pull in Irene (private deployments lead) and Laura (security/compliance) to draft the short plan for Thursday.

Cheers,
Hiro
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Team — I drafted the technical note and a proposed checklist (see attached mutual-action-plan.docx). Key decisions and recommendations in the note:

- Cluster layout: 3 Kubernetes control-plane replicas colocated across the two racks with an odd quorum (3) on dedicated control VMs (separate from GPU nodes). Use anti-affinity for control-plane pods to avoid single-rack failure.

- Node pools and Taints/Tolerations:
  * control-vm (3x small VMs, etcd + control-plane) — tainted_scheduling=controlOnly
  * infra (2x x86 infra nodes for logging/monitoring/backup agents)
  * gp-infer-rack-a (4x GPU nodes, topology.kubernetes.io/zone=rack-a)
  * gp-infer-rack-b (4x GPU nodes, topology.kubernetes.io/zone=rack-b)

- Storage strategy:
  * Local NVMe (each GPU node): model shards + KV cache (primary fast path). Use a lightweight distributed metadata catalog (local filesystem + periodic sync to object-store) to locate model shards.
  * Shared blockstore (iSCSI) for backups and long-term artifacts; nightly snapshot to your object-store.

- Networking:
  * Management VLAN for control plane; separate inference VLAN for token traffic. No cross-VLAN NAT between inference and management except for the control-plane API endpoints.
  * BGP is not required for the initial phase; we recommend static routes and a simple route reflector if you go multi-rack across aggregation switches.

- Air-gapped checklist:
  * Offline installer image (we will provide) + signed packages
  * Local package repo (you to host) or USB provisioning media for initial install
  * Telemetry policy: toggleable — by default off for fully air-gapped; can enable periodic bulk export when allowed

Open items for the Thursday review:
1) NVMe capacity: the attached node-profiles sheet shows 2TB NVMe per node; confirm this meets your model shard requirements or whether we should plan for a shared SSD tier.
2) Backup SLA to object-store: frequency and encryption mode for nightly snapshots.
3) Network ACLs: we need an allowlist for management IPs and FQDNs for out-of-band updates.

I've attached the mutual action plan and added line items for the above. Please review and add comments.

-Irene

Thanks, Irene — very helpful. Quick answers inline:

1) NVMe: 2TB per node is OK for initial pilots; we expect to add a shared SSD tier when we onboard larger models in Q4.
2) Backups: nightly encrypted snapshots to our internal S3-compatible store; retention 90 days; AES-256 server-side recommended.
3) Network ACLs: I'll send a follow-up with IPs for the management VLAN. We will not allow outbound telemetry by default; we prefer the signed offline installer route.

Two clarifications:
- Can Redwood support model pinning to specific racks for latency-sensitive workloads? We need control to bind certain models to rack-a only.
- What is the expected failover behavior if an entire rack is unreachable — do we drain the local KV cache and fallback to shared blockstore (and what's the expected token-latency delta)?

If we can cover those on Thursday, I think we're in good shape to proceed to preflight.

Best,
Tom

Subject: RE: Anchorage Health — on-prem cluster architecture & node-grid alignment

Tom — quick answers below and a proposed measurable SLA for the pilot:

- Model pinning: yes. We support topology-aware scheduling with nodeSelector + node affinity rules; we can bundle a small controller to surface model-to-node mappings and an operator for pinned deployments. We'll include a runbook for pinning/unpinning during maintenance windows.

- Rack failure fallback:
  * On rack loss we recommend the following sequence:
    1) K8s node controller marks GPU nodes NotReady; pods are rescheduled to the surviving rack if capacity exists.
    2) For KV cache: we treat local cache as ephemeral. On failover, requests will hit the shared blockstore (iSCSI) and the model artifacts already replicated to shared storage.
    3) Expected latency delta: from typical local-NVMe path (~20-30ms end-to-end token latency in our pilot footprint) to shared-blockstore path (~60-80ms) depending on your switch fabric. We will run a network-latency microbenchmark in preflight to provide numbers scoped to your switches.

Pilot SLA (proposed):
- Availability: 99.5% per week for inference nodes (excluding scheduled maintenance)
- Recovery: automatic failover to surviving rack within 90s for control-plane detection + reschedule window; dependent on available spare capacity

Next steps: schedule the Thursday technical review at 2pm PT. We'll bring a short preflight checklist and plan a 30-minute microbenchmark during the window.

Thanks — Marissa
